text: This assembly will hear an address by
his excellency Francis Evelyn Vat
Carval,
Prime Minister and Minister of Finance
of the Republic of Kabu.
I request protocol to escort his
excellency and invite him to address the
assembly.
Mr. President of the General Assembly,
Mr. Secretary General of the United
Nations. Excellencies, ladies and
gentlemen,
it is a pleasure to be here representing
Kabu Veri in this forum where the world
comes together to discuss the challenges
we share and the future we want to
build.
I come from a country made up of 10
islands in the Midatlantic.
A country aware of its vulnerabilities,
but one that has learned that the size
of a territory must never determine the
size of our dreams. The history of Kabu
is also a history of learning. We have
learned to confront drought and scarcity
to transform
sea from a barrier into a bridge. But
above all, we have learned that a
nation's greatest wealth lies in its
people. We even have a word for this
wealth which is morabaza.
A term that defines the cordiality,
determination and kindness of our people
which the world was able to witness a
little during the this year's football
world cup. Amila Cabral one of the
greatest figures of our history left us
a lesson that continues to resonate
across generations. Learn in life, learn
from our people, learn from the books
and learn from the experiences of
others. learn always. Perhaps this is an
ability that the world must rediscover.
The ability to learn from history, to
learn from one another, and to
understand that there can be no lasting
development without peace, just as there
can be no lasting peace where poverty,
exclusion, and lack of opportunity
persists. In this spirit, Kabu verdi
reaffirms its faith in the United States
in dialogue among nations, in
cooperation among peoples and in the
primacy of law over the use of force in
the face of wars, inequalities and
crisis confronting our world. We
reaffirm our unwavering commitment to
the charter of the United Nations, to
the sovereignty and territorial
integrity of states, to the protection
of civilian populations, and to the
peaceful resolution of conflicts.
International law and international
humanitarian law cannot be applied in a
selective manner. They will only be
truly and and fulfill their role when
they are respected and upheld by all. In
our region, terrorism, violent
extremism, and national crimes also
remind us that peace requires
prevention, strong institutions, and
cooperation, and requires opportunities.
Africa is the continent with the
youngest population in the world.
Therefore, investing in our young
people, in education, in knowledge, and
in the possibility of building a
dignified life means also investing in
peace. Excellencies, learning also means
embracing change. The world of today is
not the world of 1945.
The institutions were created to respond
to the challenges of that time. Need to
learn in the world that has changed.
Kabo Verde therefore supports a United
Nations that is more effective, more
transparent and more representative. The
UN AD initiative presents an opportunity
to modernize this organization and
strengthen its response capacity. In
this spirit, we also support the reform
of the security council. Africa is home
to nearly one quarter of the member
states of this organization and
represents appro approximately 1ifth of
the world's population and yet it still
lacks the representation it deserves on
this council. Therefore, we support a
more equitable African representation in
accordance with the Azawini consensus
and the third declaration. A fairer
international order also requires fairer
and more inclusive institutions. The
election of the next sec secretary
general should reflect the same
principles transparency, inclusion,
merit, merit and equal opportunities.
Ladies and gentlemen, but United Nations
is not just a place where we discuss
crisis. It is also a space where we
build common paths.
The 2030 agenda. The African Union's
agenda 2063 and the pact for the future
points us in one clear direction.
Sustainable development centered on the
people capable of trans transforming
global commitments into concrete changes
in the lives of populations.
This is also the mission of the new
government of Kabo Verdei to concretely
improve the lives of its people and we
have placed education at the heart of
this mission because school is where a
society begins to shape its future and
education is a powerful development
strategy. We seek to transform knowledge
into innovation, decent employment and
opportunities to strengthen our
education and health systems and to
advance progresses in digital
transformation,
gender equality,
energy transition, water security and
also in blue economy.
We want to create more opportunities for
our young people and build an economy
capable of transforming people's talent
into development. Development means
transforming knowledge into opportunity
and opportunity into dignity.
Excellencies for Cabo and other small
island states, the climate crisis is not
a distant threat. It is a present
reality.
Climate crisis is here. The droughts,
the desertification, water scarcity,
ocean
acid acidification and the rising sea
levels. Just look at what is happening
currently on the island of Sal where
only two days ago rising sea waters
flooded the avenue in front of the
hotels.
It is also a question of justice.
Because those who have contributed the
least to this crisis cannot continue to
bear some of its most serious
consequences.
Science has shown us the way forward. We
must translate this valuable knowledge
into decisions and actions and Kabui has
tried to do its part. In September 2024,
Kabui launched a call for a global
compact for climate mobility. And in
June in Berlin, 57 countries endorsed
the global consensus on the principles
to address climate mobility.
And at the United Nations, Kabu
facilitated negotiations on the
political declaration of the third
conference on the oceans and the
declaration on sea level rise.
Because a country made up of islands,
protecting the ocean is not just an
environmental policy.
It's a question of protecting national
territory, the economy, the culture, and
the future.
In January 2027, Kabu will take over the
presidency of the Alliance of Small
Island States, AOSIs. We will take on
this responsibility by working for the
unity of small island small island
states, the implementation of the
Antigua and Barbuda agenda for fear of
financing for climate adaptation and for
ensuring that the oceans oceans remain
at the heart of the global agenda.
In 2034, we will host the fifth
international conference on small island
developing states. This is an
opportunity
to share experiences, build common
responses and transform vulnerabilities
into opportunities.
Ladies and gentlemen, there is also
pedagogy in the relations between
nations and it begins with the ability
to listen to listen to each other. It
entails the humility to recognize that
no country alone has all the answers.
And it only makes sense when what we
learn together is translated into
action. Because this is after all the
true essence of multilateralism.
In a time of fragmentation, we need to
regain trust. In a time of
confrontation, we need to strengthen
cooperation. In a time when force so
often prevails, we need to reaffirm the
law.
Cabo is a small country, but our history
has taught us to engage in dialogue, to
build bridges, and to seek consensus.
Our history also taught us that no
country is too small to have a voice and
no challenge is too big to tackle when
we work together. The United Nations
must continue to be the space for this
collective endeavor. And I will recall
what Amila Cabral taught us. Learn
always.
Learning today also means
understanding that educating a child,
providing opportunities for young
people, protecting our planet, fighting
poverty, promoting development and
building peace are not separate
missions.
They are indeed different ways of us
caring for the future.
And perhaps this is the greatest lesson
that our times require of us. The future
is not simply what we receive.
Rather, it is what we are able to teach,
to learn and build together.
